title: Global estimates of mortality associated with long-term exposure to outdoor fine particulate matter
notes: GEMM source for PM2.5 mortality concentration-response functions

author: Khreis H, Kelly C, Tate J, et al.
title: Exposure to traffic-related air pollution and risk of development of childhood asthma: A systematic review and meta-analysis
notes: Underlying source for the NO2 childhood asthma incidence association. Paper reports OR 1.05 (1.02-1.07) per 4 ug/m3; legacy RR 1.26 (1.10-1.37) per 10 ppb is the rescaled value (1 ppb = 1.88 ug/m3, 25C), not a figure stated in the paper. Achakulwisut et al. (2019) documents the historical HIA use of this value and defines the 2 ppb counterfactual; the 1-18 age range is an HIA-model population, not a boundary stated by Khreis.

author: Achakulwisut P, Brauer M, Hystad P, Anenberg SC
title: Global, national, and urban burdens of paediatric asthma incidence attributable to ambient NO2 pollution: estimates from global datasets
notes: Historical HIA implementation source for paediatric asthma incidence: applies the Khreis-derived RR 1.26 (1.10-1.37) per 10 ppb to ages 1-18 and defines the 2 ppb counterfactual as the fifth percentile of the minimum exposure concentrations in the Khreis studies. It does not support asthma prevalence.

author: Zheng X-Y, Ding H, Jiang L-N, et al.
title: Association between Air Pollutants and Asthma Emergency Room Visits and Hospital Admissions in Time Series Studies: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
notes: Source for PM2.5 and O3 asthma ERV CRFs. L03 matches Zheng PM2.5 child subgroup; adult-labelled L04 (PM2.5) and L06 (O3) match Zheng overall estimates, not adult subgroup estimates. L05's exact O3 parameter provenance is unverified: its central value matches Zheng overall O3 after unit conversion, but the child-labelled confidence interval has not been traced. The paper does not define CREAHIA numeric age bounds; retain counterfactual and Registry age semantics as separate legacy/model decisions before migration.

author: Faustini A, Rapp R, Forastiere F
title: Nitrogen dioxide and mortality: review and meta-analysis of long-term studies
notes: Source for the C40 and South Africa NO2 mortality CRFs. The pooled estimates match the legacy all-cause RR 1.04 (1.02-1.06), cardiovascular RR 1.13 (1.09-1.18), and respiratory RR 1.03 (1.02-1.03) per 10 ug/m3. The source does not by itself approve the legacy 25-99 age range, YLL application, 4.5 ug/m3 counterfactual, or final overlap rules.

author: Trasande L, Malecha P, Attina TM
title: Particulate Matter Exposure and Preterm Birth: Estimates of U.S. Attributable Burden and Economic Costs
notes: Source identified for the PM2.5 preterm-birth legacy row: base-case OR is 1.15 per 10 ug/m3 and reference level is 8.8 ug/m3. Values 1.07 and 1.16 are low- and high-end scenario inputs, not a confidence interval. The Registry migration must resolve both whether the legacy log-linear RR calculation may use the reported odds ratio unchanged and how scenario values are represented.

author: Dadvand P, Parker J, Bell ML, et al.
title: Maternal Exposure to Particulate Air Pollution and Term Birth Weight: A Multi-Country Evaluation of Effect and Heterogeneity
notes: Source identified for the PM2.5 term low-birth-weight legacy row: it reports OR 1.10 (1.03-1.18) per 10 ug/m3 during the entire pregnancy. The legacy 4 ug/m3 counterfactual and use of the odds ratio in a log-linear RR calculation remain separate decisions before migration.

author: WHO Regional Office for Europe
title: Health risks of air pollution in Europe – HRAPIE project: recommendations for concentration–response functions for cost–benefit analysis of particulate matter, ozone and nitrogen dioxide
notes: Primary HRAPIE source. For PM2.5 work days lost: short-term Group B* CRF RR 1.046 (1.039-1.053) at ages 20-65, using a two-week average converted to annual-average PM2.5; estimated work days lost should be subtracted from restricted activity days before burden calculations to avoid double counting. For annual-mean NO2 long-term mortality: RR 1.055 (1.031-1.080) per 10 ug/m3 for all natural-cause mortality at ages 30+ and concentrations above 20 ug/m3, with Group B* treatment for potential overlap with PM2.5 mortality. Legacy outcome and adjusted values remain separate CREA implementation decisions.

author: Krewski D, Jerrett M, Burnett RT, et al.
title: Extended Follow-Up and Spatial Analysis of the American Cancer Society Study Linking Particulate Air Pollution and Mortality
notes: Source table reports all-cause mortality HR 1.020 (1.014-1.026) for SO2 (1980), matching the legacy RR per 5 ppb. The ACS CPS-II cohort enrolled adults aged 30 years and older. The paper does not define the legacy NCD.LRI outcome, 25-99 metadata, YLL application, near-zero counterfactual, or ug-to-ppb multiplier.

author: Turner MC, Jerrett M, Pope CA III, et al.
title: Long-Term Ozone Exposure and Mortality in a Large Prospective Study
journal: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
notes: Primary source of the annual daily maximum 8-h ozone HR 1.12 (1.08-1.16) per 10 ppb for respiratory mortality. This estimate is from a model adjusted for near-source PM2.5, regional PM2.5, and NO2. That adjustment supports, but does not by itself prove, an overlap-safe combination with other pollutant burdens. The Registry migration must not mislabel it as a COPD-specific effect without an explicit decision.

author: Malley CS, Henze DK, Kuylenstierna JCI, et al.
title: Updated Global Estimates of Respiratory Mortality in Adults ≥30 Years of Age Attributable to Long-Term Ozone Exposure
notes: Global burden implementation using the multipollutant-adjusted Turner respiratory-mortality HR for adults aged 30 years and older. It separately estimates COPD as a subset of respiratory mortality; its COPD estimate is about 70-71% of estimated O3-attributable respiratory mortality, which contextualises outcome coverage but is not a direct bias estimate for applying HR 1.12 to COPD baseline. Its main Turner-based calculation uses annual daily maximum 8-h ozone with a 26.7 ppb low-concentration cutoff, not the legacy 35 ppb setting.

author: Burnett RT, Spadaro JV, Garcia GR, Pope CA III
title: Designing health impact functions to assess marginal changes in outdoor fine particulate matter
notes: Primary methods paper for the Fusion PM2.5 mortality model. The current generation code returns curves from generate_rr_fusion_from_code(), which uses the Burnett-supplied "Fusion Parameters Jul 7, 2021.csv" and "LL Fusion Parameters theta eq 97.5.csv". The packaged rr/processed/rr_fusion.csv is the migration source, but its Git history does not establish regeneration by the current code. The lookup workbook is a validation reference only; workbook metadata identifies Joseph V. Spadaro as its creator, and the code notes that generated values do not yet exactly match it.

author: Global Burden of Disease Collaborative Network
title: Global Burden of Disease Study 2019 (GBD 2019) Particulate Matter Risk Curves
journal: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME)
notes: Official IHME dataset for the GBD 2019 particulate-matter risk curves. The packaged rr/processed/rr_gbd2019.csv is the direct migration source. The original downloaded IHME files are not versioned in this repository, and Git history does not establish regeneration of the packaged CSV by the current generate_rr_gbd2019() code. YLL and YLD rows apply the death curves, as in historical CREA workflows. LRI.child is created locally by add_lri_child() from the processed LRI curve and is not an independently downloaded child-specific curve.

author: Global Burden of Disease Collaborative Network
title: Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 (GBD 2023) Air Pollution Exposure Estimates and Risk Curves 1990-2023
journal: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME)
notes: Official IHME dataset for the GBD 2023 air pollution risk curves. In the packaged rr/processed/rr_gbd2023.csv, Dementia is regenerated from the official 2025 mean file by generate_rr_gbd2023(). IHD, LRI and Stroke come from the earlier 2024 GBD 2023 files, on a different exposure grid, and match the official release within 1e-4 RR. COPD, Diabetes and LC are the GBD 2021 curves, re-released as is in GBD 2023. YLL and YLD rows apply the death curves, as in historical CREA workflows. LRI.child is created locally by add_lri_child() from the processed LRI curve and is not an independently downloaded child-specific curve.
